candidates.text:
Some career moves are less about where you wish to go and more about the difference you hope to make along the way.

This next chapter feels like one such move.

Back in April, I stumbled upon an article by Tigerfeathers on @dognosis, and I couldn’t stop thinking about one question:

What can a dog’s nose tell us about cancer in humans? 

Fascinated by the idea of harnessing canine olfaction with the help of AI, I reached out to the team over email. A few months later, here I am, joining Dognosis as a Brand Lead. 

It’s not every day that you get to work at the intersection of science, technology, and our four-legged best friends to address a challenge that affects so many lives.

Here’s to following your curiosity and seeing where it takes you.

Curious? Join the CancerWatch waitlist: https://t.co/cIIxZuZzQC

candidates.text:
It's a difficult time for anyone who provides shitty service yet still charges a subscription.

Whatever parts of the economy haven't been touched by AI or some version of AI tooling, a human empowered with AI will provide better service for a lower price.

I see it everywhere, from the clunkiest industries like short-term rental management to freight brokerage.

Bad products are being flushed out of the market faster than before.

This matters because if you think you can acquire a company, cut all costs, and keep making money, you will get humbled quickly.

I've seen cases where revenue drops by 50% in less than 1 year. Your lock-in is being a good product and delivering more value than before.

This is just the beginning of a new era of software or software + services.

candidates.text:
Today I tried to articulate something on a call that I've been trying to figure out, as my O-1 is up for renewal and I'm thinking about applying for an EB-1A (a green card, essentially). 

I was talking about how culturally different living in the US is. Being British, and having lived in France before this, France felt culturally more like home to me despite it not being my first language. America feels further removed, despite being an English-speaking country. 

It's still something I really struggle to articulate, and I think it just came up very emotionally, again because I'm still thinking about it. How isolating it can feel here. How misunderstood you can feel. And it's something I, and the people around me, don't think about, because it doesn't seem like such a big issue on the surface. It's like, well, at least it's still English, right? It's kind of odd sometimes. 

Why do we move so far away to try to achieve things, just to not achieve them?
